SMTO-KV-0001 — The agent's note request used a number SMTO can't accept

GUID: e3f97d63-825c-4cdb-b57a-cc30f60866ce
Slug: kv-invalid-argument
Domain: KV · Subsystem: kv

What happened

  • The agent keeps short notes for this task in the Task Scratchpad. One of its note requests used a number SMTO can't accept, such as zero or a page size that's too big, so nothing was saved or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the agent continue; it usually corrects the number and tries the note again. The rejected request didn't change any notes, so correcting it is safe.
  2. If it keeps failing, tell the agent to save its note without an expiry time, or to read the note again first so it uses the note's current version. A wrong expiry time or version number is the usual cause, and reading the note first avoids overwriting someone else's change.
  3. If this appeared while you were deleting a conversation, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. In that case the problem is inside SMTO, not in anything you or the agent typed.

What success looks like

  • The agent carries on without this error and its note steps show as completed.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO. Don't edit or delete SMTO's data files to clear this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Agent KV rejected a non-integer, boolean, non-positive or over-limit argument (limit, expected_revision or ttl_seconds), or an internal conversation-delete call passed an unsupported KV database alias.

What this means

  • KV validation rejects a non-integer, boolean, nonpositive or excessive revision/page value; an internal conversation-delete call also rejects an unsupported database schema selector. KV checks apply only to the selected conversation. Rejected validation or compare-and-set does not authorize an unconditional replacement; diagnostics do not read or mutate additional stored values.

Why this can happen

  • KV validation rejects a non-integer, boolean, nonpositive or excessive revision/page value; an internal conversation-delete call also rejects an unsupported database schema selector.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the named argument; a bad internal schema selector requires caller repair rather than changing a stored value.

How to fix it

  • Pass exact positive integers: list limit ≤ 100, search limit ≤ 25, ttl_seconds ≤ 315360000, and expected_revision taken from a prior read. If the message is "Invalid KV database alias", fix the internal caller of KVStore.delete_conversation_in (schema must be kv_db or main) rather than editing conversation data.
  • Correct the reported revision/page argument; if an internal schema selector caused this error, repair that caller rather than editing conversation data.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported scoped operation validates its actual argument contract.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • KV checks apply only to the selected conversation. Rejected validation or compare-and-set does not authorize an unconditional replacement; diagnostics do not read or mutate additional stored values.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
